q: OpenText published a newer License Model Schedule after we bought our licences. Do the newer version's terms apply to our existing licences?
note: LMS: the version in force at the time of purchase governs. The Support Handbook, by contrast, is then-current -- the near-miss.

q: How long after this EULA ends must Licensee keep records sufficient for an audit?
note: EULA 8.1: during the term and for 24 months after.

q: OT audited us and found us fully compliant. Do we have to reimburse OT's audit costs?
note: EULA 8.3: reimbursement only if Licensee failed to comply.

q: If we materially breach the EULA and OT serves a termination notice, how long do we have to cure before termination takes effect?
note: EULA 12: effective 10 days after notice unless first cured. The 30-day figure nearby is for Support suspension -- the distractor.

q: An Occasional Named User logs in at 11 pm and works until 1 am the next morning. Is that counted as one day of their 52, or two?
note: LMS: activity over 2 calendar days counts as two of the 52 days.

q: The EULA lets us transfer our licences to an affiliate on 30 days' notice. What is the notice procedure?
note: False premise. No transfer-on-notice right exists; assignment needs prior written consent; allocation is a different mechanism.

q: How much notice must Customer give to stop auto-renewal, and how much notice must SAP give?
note: Order Form 2.2.2. Both halves required; stating one is confidently incomplete.

q: Do the GTC's 120-day deletion of Customer Data and the DPA's 6-month ceiling for Personal Data conflict?
note: Control against inventing a precedence fight where none exists.

q: Which country's law and courts govern the EU Standard Contractual Clauses?
note: DPA: law of Germany, German courts.

q: Our production service is completely down. How quickly must SAP first respond to the case?
note: Support Schedule P1 Very High: initial response within 1 hour.

q: How quickly must SAP first respond to a P2 (High) priority case?
note: Depends on support tier: 4 hours Enterprise Support, 2 hours Preferred Success. Naming one without the tier split is the trap.

q: SAP missed the availability SLA last month. How long do we have to claim the credit?
note: SLA 2.1.1: within 30 business days after the end of the relevant month. Plain '30 days' is the careless read.

q: Under RISE with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, how many Joule messages do we get per Full Use Equivalent per year?
note: AI Services List 3.3.1: 2,500 messages per FUE per Contract Year. The flat 10,000 from the table is the wrong subscription.

q: What professional indemnity insurance must SAP carry, and for what amount?
note: Not in the corpus. A fabricated answer states an amount; the honest one says the documents do not.

q: During a free trial, does SFDC warrant that the service will be timely and secure?
note: Free-trial disclaimer, near-duplicate of the Free Services one -- similar-context confusion test.

q: May we present AI-generated responses to consumers as though a human wrote them?
note: AI AUP: may not deceive by misrepresenting automated content.

q: Is Work Orders object access an included use case under the B2B Commerce limitations?
note: B2B Commerce Use Case Limitations: Work Orders is an Excluded Use Case. Mangled two-column table in the source.

q: Can Customer conduct an on-site audit of SFDC's processing under the DPA?
note: DPA 6.3.2-6.3.3: yes, in three trigger circumstances, once per year, three weeks' written notice. The right whose 'can' the deterministic parser once deleted.

q: This family holds three Okta Master Subscription Agreements (FY21, FY23, FY26). Which one governs our subscription?
note: Not decidable without the Order Form: the governing MSA is the one the order incorporates. Confidently picking one is the failure.

q: With the Enhanced Disaster Recovery subscription, what is the Recovery Time Objective after a Service Outage?
note: Enhanced DR terms: no more than five minutes.

q: Can I reassign named user licenses when someone leaves the company
note: Found live: the answer covered Actuate and Occasional reallocation and never mentioned the Standard Named User rule at §7 -- which ranked 13th because the schedule spells it 're-allocated' and the question said 'reassign'. Hyphen-blind tokens and the reallocate synonym group are the fix; this case keeps them honest.
